front: What is a coordinate system in 3D?
back: Three mutually perpendicular lines (x-axis, y-axis, z-axis) meeting at the origin O, forming a right-handed rectangular coordinate system.

front: How many coordinate planes are there?
back: 3: XY-plane (z=0), YZ-plane (x=0), ZX-plane (y=0). Each pair of axes forms one plane.
8 octants, formed by the three coordinate planes. Each octant is identified by the signs of (x, y, z).
(+, +, +) — all coordinates positive. Octants I–IV have z > 0; V–VIII have z < 0.
PQ = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁) + (z₂−z₁)²) — extension of the 2D formula using Pythagorean theorem twice.

front: Distance from origin to P(x, y, z)

back: x-axis: (a, 0, 0). y-axis: (0, b, 0). z-axis: (0, 0, c). Two coordinates are always zero.

front: How to verify a parallelogram in 3D
back: Check that both pairs of opposite sides are equal using the distance formula: AB = CD and BC = DA.
